payload.excerpt: A machine that applies pressure to transfer ink onto paper — invented by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440 and the start of mass communication in Europe.

blocks.text: A printing press applies pressure to transfer ink onto **paper, cloth, or a similar material**. It replaced the older method of rubbing paper by hand to pick up ink.

blocks.definition: A machine that applies pressure to transfer ink onto paper, cloth, or a similar material; invented by the German goldsmith Johannes Gutenberg around 1440.

cites.quote: A printing press is a machine that applies pressure to transfer ink onto a surface made of paper, cloth, or a similar material.
It marked a significant improvement on earlier methods, in which the paper was rubbed by hand to transfer applied ink to the printing surface.
The printing press was invented by the German goldsmith Johannes Gutenberg around 1440

blocks.text: Gutenberg's press was an integration, not a single invention. He took four technologies already in use and built them into one working system.

items: Screw press — direct pressure on a flat plane; already used for wine and oil.
Movable type — individual reusable characters; East Asian versions were relatively inefficient.
Codex — the book format, in use since the Roman Empire.
Papermaking — mechanized production; water-powered mills by 1282.

cites.quote: Gutenberg invented the movable-type printing press around 1440, utilizing four existing technologies: the screw press, movable type, the codex book format, and mechanized paper production.
Gutenberg integrated these four technologies into a single working system
The first factor, the screw press, permitted direct pressure to be applied on a flat plane.
Movable type is the typographical principle of writing a text from individual reusable characters.
The codex book format also dated to the Roman Empire
Water-powered paper mills were in usage by 1282

blocks.text: The press did not create demand from nothing. Late medieval Europe already had conditions that made a commercial print shop viable.

items: Urban middle class grew alongside trade and commerce.
Universities, growing since the twelfth century, increased demand for books.
By the fifteenth century, manuscript supply was much less than demand.

blocks.text: Gutenberg's contribution was the integration — plus his own hand mold for casting type and an oil-based ink suited to metal type.

cites.quote: The urban middle class grew alongside trade and commerce, while the growing number of universities since the twelfth century had increased demand for books.
Hand-copying was slow and expensive, and by the fifteenth century, the supply of manuscripts was much less than the demand.
